improvements.description: Define key bootstrap and distribution procedure for new operators/machines, including how the maintainer offline root key is initially generated, escrowed, and recovered if the maintainer becomes unavailable.
improvements.rationale: Section 1.9.3.1 requires every audit log to verify against the trust-store signed by an offline root key, but provides no bus-factor mitigation. If the maintainer loses the root key or is unavailable, no trust-store updates are possible and key rotation halts indefinitely. This is a single point of failure for the entire signing scheme.

improvements.description: Specify the exact byte-level canonicalization input for `prev_hash` and signature computation (field ordering, payload nesting, Unicode normalization, number representation) and provide a worked example with hex bytes alongside the conformance vectors.
improvements.rationale: Section 3.2.1 describes prev_hash as 'SHA-256 of canonical-JSON of prior entry's content (excluding signature + signing_key_id)' but this still leaves ambiguity about whether `redaction_applied: null` is included, how floating-point payload numbers are serialized under JCS, and whether nested payload sub-objects are recursively canonicalized. Cross-implementation hash drift will silently break chains. A worked example with bytes is the only unambiguous spec.

improvements.description: Add explicit threat model for the machine-fingerprint check, including what attack it does and does not prevent (e.g., it does not prevent a single-machine attacker with filesystem access from forging entries; an operator who copies `.run/machine-fingerprint` along with audit logs bypasses the check).
improvements.rationale: Section 1.7.1 introduces fingerprint guardrails as a 'hard runtime guardrail' but the fingerprint file is itself untracked and unsigned. An operator copying the entire `.run/` directory to a second machine bypasses the check trivially. The SDD presents this as a security boundary when it is really a foot-gun preventer. Mis-stating the threat model invites over-reliance.

improvements.description: Specify concrete latency/SLO measurement methodology and CI gating thresholds for write-path SLOs (audit log append p95 <50ms, p99 <200ms) — including measurement environment, sample size, what counts as a 'write', and what happens when CI exceeds threshold.
improvements.rationale: The v1.2 changelog cites IMP-005 as adding 'latency/SLO targets for write path' but the body only mentions them in passing. Without measurement methodology (cold vs warm cache, with/without flock contention, signing key cache state), the SLO is unenforceable. Ed25519 signing + ajv validation + flock + jq canonical-JSON + git history check on every append is a non-trivial budget for 50ms p95.

improvements.description: Define the tool-resolver provenance-tagging mechanism concretely: where `provenance: untrusted-session-start` metadata is stored, how the tool resolver introspects it, and what 'first N turns' means operationally. Provide an enforcement test case.
improvements.rationale: Section 1.9.3.2 Layer 5 describes deny-by-default tool resolution as the load-bearing security boundary, but the implementation is vague ('heuristic: any tool call within first N turns'). N is not defined; persistence of the provenance tag across context compaction is not specified; integration with Loa's existing tool-call harness is not described. Without a concrete mechanism this is aspirational, not implemented.

improvements.description: Add explicit specification for L2 cost-budget behavior when multiple cycles run concurrently on the same machine (e.g., L3 nightly cron + interactive operator session). Define whether the counter is per-process, shared via flock, and how race conditions on the warn-90/halt-100 threshold are resolved.
improvements.rationale: Section 1.4.2 L2 describes per-cycle and per-session tracking but the system explicitly supports concurrent L3 schedules and operator sessions. Two near-simultaneous paid calls each reading 89% usage could both decide 'allow' and push the day over 100%. The fail-closed guarantee (G-2) is undermined without a documented locking discipline on the counter.

improvements.description: Specify the per-event-type payload schema registry mechanism: where schemas live, naming convention, validation gate (CI vs runtime), version evolution rules, and what happens when an unknown event_type is encountered on read.
improvements.rationale: v1.1 changelog cites IMP-001 'per-event-type payload schemas + schema registry pattern + CI validation step' but Section 3.2 only enumerates event_type examples. There is no schema for any specific event_type body, no registry path stated, and no read-side handling for unknown types. This is the crux of long-term schema evolution and is currently unresolved despite being marked integrated.

improvements.description: Provide a concrete L4 trust ledger merge/conflict resolution algorithm for the documented divergent-valid-chains case, including the merge marker injection format, the operator arbitration UI, and how chain integrity is restored post-merge.
improvements.rationale: v1.2 changelog cites IMP-003 'git-backed conflict resolution protocol for divergent valid chains' as integrated, but Section 3.4 does not contain this protocol — only the §3.4.4 hash-chain recovery for tampering. The trust ledger is the one tracked-in-git audit log, so git merge conflicts are the most likely real-world failure mode and need explicit handling.

improvements.description: Replace `jq -S -c` references in the glossary and Section 2.2 with consistent RFC 8785 JCS terminology, since the v1.2 SKP-004 explicitly removes `jq -S -c` as a canonicalization mechanism but the body and appendix still reference it.
improvements.rationale: v1.2 changelog states 'Removes jq -S -c references' and 'Mixed-mode verification rejected', but Section 2.2 still lists 'Canonical JSON via jq -S -c' as a backend technology, Appendix A glossary defines canonical-JSON as 'Computed via jq -S -c', and the bats test in Section 7.2.1 uses `jq -S -c` to compute hash. This contradiction will cause implementer confusion and the conformance vectors will not match.

improvements.description: Add an integration test specification (or explicit deferral) for the maintainer offline-root-key signing workflow, including how the test exercises the offline ceremony without exposing real keys, and how CI verifies the pinned root pubkey integrity check.
improvements.rationale: Section 1.9.3.1 makes the offline root key the foundation of trust, with documented failure modes including 'all audit log verifications fail' on tampering. Yet Section 7 testing strategy contains no test for this critical path. Untested security ceremonies historically break silently. Either specify the test or explicitly defer with rationale.

opus_reviewer.summary: 10 improvements identified, 6 HIGH priority, 4 MEDIUM priority. Key themes: ambiguity in cryptographic canonicalization (IMP-002, IMP-009), unresolved security mechanism details (IMP-003, IMP-005, IMP-001), concurrency/integrity gaps (IMP-006, IMP-008), and integration deltas where v1.1/v1.2 changelog claims are not fully reflected in the body (IMP-007, IMP-008, IMP-009).

concerns.concern: Scope is enormous: 7 independent skills + 5 cross-cutting infrastructure libraries + Ed25519 signing + hash chains + trust store with offline root + jailbreak CI suite + machine fingerprinting, all in 6-10 weeks
concerns.why_matters: Each of these subsystems alone (e.g., a signed audit log with key rotation/revocation/recovery) is typically a multi-month project. Sprint 1 alone bundles audit envelope + JCS + Ed25519 + trust store + offline root signing + protected class router + operator identity + tier validator + L1 panel skill. Historical software patterns suggest this slips by 2-3x. The 'Sprint 4.5 buffer week' is wildly inadequate. R11 acknowledges this but mitigations are aspirational (de-scope triggers, weekly check-ins) rather than structural.
concerns.recommendation: Hard cut scope: ship L1+L6+L7 with a minimal HMAC-chain (no Ed25519, no trust store, no offline root) as v1; defer L2-L5 and full signing infrastructure to a v2 cycle. Or extend timeline to 16-20 weeks honestly.

concerns.concern: Offline root key for trust-store creates a single human bottleneck with no documented succession or availability SLA
concerns.why_matters: §1.9.3.1 says 'maintainer offline → cannot sign updates → freeze new key issuance until next maintainer window.' If the maintainer is unavailable (vacation, illness, departure, lost YubiKey), no one can rotate keys, onboard operators, or respond to compromise. A compromised key during maintainer absence becomes catastrophic. There is no M-of-N threshold scheme, no documented succession, no break-glass procedure. The pinned root pubkey at .claude/data/maintainer-root-pubkey.txt is itself in a git-writable file, only protected by 'reviewer-only edits' which is a social control, not cryptographic.
concerns.recommendation: Use M-of-N threshold signatures (e.g., 2-of-3 maintainers) or document explicit break-glass procedure with time-bounded recovery. Cryptographically pin root pubkey via signed release artifact, not a git-mutable file.

concerns.concern: Hash-chain recovery via git history is fundamentally unsound for files that are explicitly UNTRACKED
concerns.why_matters: §3.4.4 says recovery walks `git log -p <log_file>` to rebuild broken chains. But §3.7 declares .run/panel-decisions.jsonl, .run/cost-budget-events.jsonl, etc. as UNTRACKED. There is no git history for these files. The 'mandatory weekly snapshot' creates a 7-day RPO during which a chain break is unrecoverable. Worse, if an attacker tampers with the live log between snapshots, the snapshot itself may not detect the gap because the snapshot is just a copy of the current (possibly tampered) state. The recovery procedure is inconsistent with the persistence policy.
concerns.recommendation: Either track all chain-integrity-critical logs in git (with the operational pain that entails) or replace git-based recovery with append-only durable storage + offsite mirror. Reconcile §3.4.4 with §3.7 before implementation.

concerns.concern: Tool-call boundary defense (Layer 5, §1.9.3.2) depends on heuristics that will misfire and block legitimate work
concerns.why_matters: 'Heuristic: any tool call within first N turns where SessionStart content was present' will trigger constantly because SessionStart content is present at every session start by definition. This means every Bash/Edit/Write in the first N turns of every session will require 're-confirmation,' destroying the autonomous-operation value proposition (the whole point of the cycle per UC-1). Operators will either disable the check or build muscle memory to click through, defeating the security goal.
concerns.recommendation: Define provenance more precisely: only tool calls whose arguments derive from SessionStart-tagged content should be denied/reconfirmed, not all tool calls in early turns. This requires data-flow tracking which is significantly harder than the SDD acknowledges.

improvements.description: Resolve canonicalization inconsistency by replacing all remaining `jq -S -c` references with RFC 8785 JCS implementation details, commands, and test assertions.
improvements.rationale: The document states v1.2 unified on RFC 8785 JCS, but multiple sections (Software Stack, Data Modeling, Appendix) still prescribe `jq -S -c`, which can produce non-JCS output and break signature/hash interoperability across languages.
improvements.location: §2.2 Canonical JSON; §3.3 Canonical serialization; §7.2 test snippets; Appendix A/B

improvements.description: Define deterministic time-source and timestamp precision policy for `ts_utc` generation (clock source, monotonic guard, leap-second handling, microsecond formatting, tie-break on same-microsecond writes).
improvements.rationale: Hash-chain and signature validity depend on reproducible timestamp semantics. Ambiguity in time formatting and ordering can cause non-deterministic chains, verification disagreements, and false integrity failures.
improvements.location: §1.4.1 Audit Envelope responsibilities; §3.2.1 `ts_utc` field; §5.2 audit_emit behavior

improvements.description: Specify key-loading and trust-store verification behavior in non-interactive CI/cron contexts, including fail mode when offline root verification cannot run and explicit bootstrap path for first install.
improvements.rationale: The SDD relies on offline-root signed trust-store checks at session start but does not fully define how autonomous cron/CI runs verify trust without interactive operator context, creating deployment ambiguity and potential bypasses.
improvements.location: §1.7 Deployment in CI/cron; §1.9.3.1 Trust-store root of trust; §8 sprint acceptance criteria

improvements.description: Add explicit replay/duplication protection requirements for audit events (event UUID, nonce or monotonic sequence per log, duplicate write rejection semantics).
improvements.rationale: Hash-chaining protects order/tamper but not semantic duplicates caused by retries/crashes. Without replay controls, the system may record duplicated actions that appear validly signed and chained.
improvements.location: §1.5.1 Audit log write path; §3.2.1 envelope schema; §5.2 `audit_emit`

improvements.description: Clarify and normalize tracked path references for trust ledger (currently `.run/trust-ledger.jsonl` vs `grimoires/loa/trust-ledger.jsonl`) and define a single authoritative location with migration rules.
improvements.rationale: Conflicting file paths for a critical integrity artifact create implementation risk, backup gaps, and incorrect startup-failure checks.
improvements.location: §1.3 component diagram; §1.4 L4 responsibilities; §3.7 persistence policy table

improvements.description: Add explicit schema and validation rules for machine fingerprint generation inputs, platform-specific fallback behavior, and privacy constraints (what is stored/hashed, salting strategy, collision handling).
improvements.rationale: Current fingerprint definition is high-level and OS-dependent. Without strict normalization, legitimate same-machine runs may be blocked or, conversely, distinct hosts may collide.

improvements.description: Define immutable redaction policy versioning and verification so that redaction configuration changes cannot silently alter security posture for future writes.
improvements.rationale: Redaction is configurable per primitive, but there is no signed/versioned policy binding to events. This weakens forensic consistency and complicates audit interpretation over time.

improvements.description: Specify formal recovery safety constraints for `audit_recover_chain` (who can run it, required approvals, forbidden auto-recovery conditions, and evidentiary markers).
improvements.rationale: Recovery from git history is powerful and potentially destructive if misused. Lacking governance controls could allow accidental or malicious rewriting under the guise of recovery.

improvements.description: Add precise SLO measurement methodology and load profiles for stated latency targets (sample size, warm/cold cache, hardware baseline, CI variance thresholds).
improvements.rationale: Latency targets are present but non-testable without a measurement contract; different environments can produce conflicting pass/fail outcomes and flaky CI gates.
improvements.location: §1.8 scalability targets; §6.4 logging/latency mention; §7 testing strategy

improvements.description: Define explicit compatibility matrix and degradation behavior for external dependencies (`ajv`, `yq`, `gh`, `gpg`, Python libs), including minimum command variants and startup diagnostics.
improvements.rationale: The SDD includes fallbacks but not a complete runtime compatibility contract. Missing/variant tooling is a likely operational failure mode on macOS/Linux and CI runners.
improvements.location: §2 Software Stack; §6 Error categories (configuration/external-api); §7 CI matrix

concerns.concern: Canonicalization approach is internally inconsistent (RFC 8785 JCS claimed, but multiple sections still specify jq -S -c).
concerns.why_matters: Hashes/signatures will diverge across implementations if canonicalization is not exactly one algorithm. This can cause false chain-breaks, failed signature verification, and audit system collapse.
concerns.location: §2.2 (Canonical JSON), §3.3 (canonical serialization), Appendix A/B references to jq -S -c
concerns.recommendation: Define one normative canonicalization algorithm and remove contradictory references. Add MUST-level test vectors and fail CI if any implementation byte output differs.

concerns.concern: Single-machine assumption conflicts with stated system vision of operator-absent multi-operator/multi-repo workflows.
concerns.why_matters: Real teams will operate across multiple machines/CI runners; current design hard-refuses writes via fingerprint checks, risking operational deadlock and user workarounds that bypass safety.
concerns.recommendation: Either narrow product claims to same-machine explicitly everywhere or implement a minimal multi-host coordination strategy before rollout (canonical writer, merge protocol, shared trust-store sync).

concerns.concern: Root-of-trust bootstrap and rotation process is underspecified and operationally brittle (single maintainer offline key bottleneck).
concerns.why_matters: If maintainer unavailable or root key lost/compromised, trust-store updates stall and audit verification may halt project operation.
concerns.recommendation: Add formal root key ceremony, escrow/recovery process, quorum-based alternate signers, and explicit business-continuity runbook with tested drills.

concerns.concern: Performance/SLO targets are not credible against required cryptographic + schema-validation write path and frequent session-start processing.
concerns.why_matters: p95/p99 goals may fail under realistic log sizes and slower laptops/CI, causing perceived flakiness and pressure to disable security checks.
concerns.location: §1.4.1 audit write path, §1.8 scalability, changelog mention of write-path SLOs
concerns.recommendation: Benchmark with worst-case payloads and long chains; define degradation behavior; introduce incremental verification/indexing and explicit perf budgets per primitive.

concerns.concern: Prompt-injection defenses rely on heuristics and turn-based provenance assumptions that attackers can bypass.
concerns.why_matters: Tool-call gating tied to first-N-turn heuristics and pattern detection can miss delayed, obfuscated, or indirect injections, enabling unauthorized actions.
concerns.recommendation: Enforce provenance taint through full conversation DAG, not turn window heuristics; require explicit operator confirmation for all mutating/exfiltrating tools when untrusted context is present.

concerns.concern: Backup/recovery still accepts up to 7-day data loss for untracked critical logs, conflicting with forensic integrity goals.
concerns.why_matters: L1/L2 chain segments can be irrecoverably lost between snapshots, undermining claims of complete auditable decision history.
concerns.location: §3.7 Backup and Recovery (weekly snapshot, RPO=7 days)
concerns.recommendation: Move critical logs to tracked or near-real-time append replication; reduce RPO to <=24h (or near-zero) and validate restore procedures in CI.

concerns.concern: Integration complexity is underestimated across seven primitives with optional composition and only five tested tier combinations.
concerns.why_matters: Unsupported but possible config permutations can behave unpredictably in production; warn-mode tier enforcement allows risky combos to run anyway.
concerns.location: §1.4/§1.6 composition model, §1.4.1 tier validator, §7.2.4 tier tests
concerns.recommendation: Either hard-refuse unsupported tiers by default or dramatically expand compatibility matrix tests; add contract tests for every primitive-pair interaction.

concerns.concern: Identity verification model is weak/optional and can produce false confidence in handoff/trust decisions.
concerns.why_matters: Optional git/gpg checks and warn modes permit unverified actors to appear in key workflows, reducing non-repudiation and enabling impersonation in shared environments.
concerns.location: §1.4.1 Operator Identity Library, §1.9.1 Authentication, §5.8 L6 strict/warn modes
concerns.recommendation: Set strict identity verification defaults for sensitive operations; require cryptographic identity for trust changes and handoff authorship in production mode.

concerns.concern: L2 billing uncertainty logic and provider-lag rules are complex and likely to cause frequent false halts or operator override fatigue.
concerns.why_matters: Overly conservative fail-closed behavior without robust auto-reconciliation can repeatedly stop autonomous cycles, reducing system usefulness and encouraging unsafe bypasses.
concerns.location: §1.5.3 L2 state model, §5.4 reconciliation and uncertainty thresholds
concerns.recommendation: Calibrate thresholds with production telemetry, implement bounded auto-reconcile with safeguards, and define clear operator UX for temporary degraded operation.

concerns.concern: Timeline risk remains severe: scope includes heavy cross-cutting infra plus 7 primitives in 6-10 weeks despite prior critical schedule warnings.
concerns.why_matters: Underestimated effort can force late de-scoping or rushed security/integration work, creating long-term technical debt and unstable delivery.
concerns.recommendation: Rebaseline with explicit critical path, reduce initial scope (ship fewer primitives first), and gate later primitives on measured completion and stability metrics.
